title: Flip-flops and Counters
toolchain: no code on screen. Check every truth table, excitation table, K-map grouping, Boolean simplification and count sequence by exhaustive enumeration in Python 3.11.9, standard library only (itertools.product over the inputs): `python3 -I check.py`. No HDL simulator is installed (iverilog, yosys, ghdl, verilator: none).

sources.note: Slides for the whole course (190 pp.). This lecture is pp. 85-101, ending with p. 101's 'Synchronous Counter' (arbitrary count sequence) slide; p. 101's 'Shift Register' slide and pp. 102+ are the next lecture. pp. 78-84 (sequential logic intro, RS latch, its state transition table and state diagram) are the previous lecture: refresher (ch1 s2) and callback (ch5 s3) only. What the viewer already knows: XOR p. 15, K-maps pp. 26-36 (don't cares p. 35, prime and essential prime implicants p. 36), gate propagation delay p. 58, timing diagrams p. 60. pdftotext drops overbars: read formulas from the rendered page (pdftoppm)
